findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The soda nozzle on the soda machine at the drive-thru was observed containing soil accumulations. PIC was made aware. Ensure that food contact surfaces such as the soda nozzles are monitored, cleaned, and sanitized at a regular frequency.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspector observed dirty mop water sitting in the mop bucket by the utility sink. PIC was made aware. PIC told inspector that the mop water may have been from the night before. The mop water was disposed appropriately. Ensure that dirty water from mopping is disposed immediately after mopping at all times.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.15 Cleaning Maintenance Tools, Preventing Contamination. FOOD preparation sinks, HANDWASHING SINKS, and WAREWASHING EQUIPMENT may not be used for the cleaning of maintenance tools, the preparation or holding of maintenance materials, or the disposal of mop water and similar liquid wastes.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
The following were observed.
1. The caulking on the hand sink by the office was observed loose and not sealed to the wall. 
2. An accumulation of ice buildup was observed behind the refrigeration unit in the walk-in freezer. 
PIC was made aware. PIC assured inspector that the hand sink will be caulked and the ice accumulation cleaned. Ensure that the caulking onto hand sink is re-done and the accumulated Ice cleaned providing a smooth and easily cleanable surface.
findings.citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Several utensils in storage were observed with remaining food debris on them. The PIC confirmed that the storage location should be clean items and moved the entire container back to dish for re-cleaning. Ensure that all food contact items are completely cleaned prior to storage in the facility. It is highly suggested that the employees that conduct dish washing procedures be re-educated to ensure that all dishes are completely cleaned prior to storage moving forward.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment: Inspector observed there to be ice build-up in the standalone freezer, as well as the WIF. Ice seems to be emanating from the cooling element in both cases. Discussed with PIC, PIC informed inspector that standalone freezer had just been serviced. Ensure that it is serviced again, along with the walk-in freezer to prevent the build-up of ice in the freezers.
findings.citation_text: 4-101.19 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspector observed there to be a gap between the cove base on the mop sink, and the mop sink basin. This gap needs to be filled to create a smooth, durable, and easily cleanable surface. Discussed with PIC. Ensure this area is caulked, or the gap is otherwise filled to create a smooth, durable, and easily cleanable surface transition.

findings.comment:

6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.comment:

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. 

In walk-in units (both refrigerator and freezer) There is dust accumulation observed. In the walk-in freezer, there is small dust accumulation on the fans on the condenser. In the refrigerator there is dust accumulation on piping behind condenser as well as dust accumulation on the line containing wiring for lightbulb in unit. At this time, no contamination risk exists due to all foods being properly sealed and/or unopened in boxes. See that these areas are cleaned frequently to prevent accumulation.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.16: (A) Wall and ceiling covering materials shall be attached so that they are EASILY CLEANABLE. (B) Except in areas used only for dry storage, concrete, porous blocks, or bricks used for indoor wall construction shall be finished and SEALED to provide a SMOOTH, nonabsorbent, EASILY CLEANABLE surface. 

In area containing soda lines in back of restaurant near water heater closet- a piece of nudo board is coming off the wall, creating a considerable gap for moisture and/or pests to get inside. See that this portion of wall is repaired so wall covering is flush with wall and gap is sealed. Will follow up at next routine inspection.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. 

Observed some ice build up in the walk-in freezer both behind the condenser and around the door frame, making it difficult to close the door properly. See that the walk-in freezer is free of ice accumulation by next routine inspection. Note: this violation does not affect cold holding temperatures of TCS foods as the walk-in freezer is located within the walk-in cooler.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. 

Observed dust and debris buildup in the hood crevices above the fryers. Service sticker indicates hood cleaning was due 10-26-20 by Lindsey's II Pro Hood Cleaning. Contact hood cleaning company and schedule a routine cleaning. Will check at next routine inspection.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.12  (C) In-Use Utensils are stored incorrectly. Store in-use utensils: 1) in the food with the handle above the top of the food item; 2) on a clean and sanitized surface; 3) in running water; 4) in a container of hot water maintained at or above 135 °F. Reference 3-304.12.

Observed scoops for shredded cheese in the prep line with handles in contact with food. Ensure all handles are kept out of food to prevent contamination. PIC removed the handles from the cheese.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13  (C) Soil residue present on fans in walk-in cooler. Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

Observed dust accumulation on fans in walk-in cooler. Ensure debris is cleaned off fans routinely to prevent from being blown onto food in the cooler. Will check next routine inspection. Discussed with person in charge.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114 Bleach solution in sani-bucket by the front make line handsink was less than 100ppm. Solution was discarded and new solution prepared at proper concentration of 100ppm. 

A chemical sanitizer shall be used in accordance with EPA-registered label use instructions. Maintain solutions at 100ppm per label instructions, and use test strips to verify concentration.
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 (E)(4) Lower left edge of the drive thru soda machine ice shoot had mold accumulation. Ice shoot was sanitized during the inspection. 
Lobby soda machine was observed with heavy mold accumulation where nozzles attach to the machine. Manager sanitized the area in question during the inspection. 

Equipment such as beverage dispensing nozzles and ice shoots of soda machines shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Gloves used properly
findings.citation_text:
3-304.15 - Employee did not change gloves after handling boxes of recently delivered dry goods and prior to returning to the make line. Employee washed hands and changed gloves at the request of the manager.

Men's room handsink and inside the toilet were soiled with general buildup. Clean in the restrooms daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

750-1120c Sinks used for food preparation or for washing equipment or utensils shall not be used for hand washing.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
750.650a  - Clean dish drying racks above 3 part sink had sections where paint has chipped away and rust is beginning to form. Replace the drying racks.

Food contact surfaces shall be smooth, non absorbent, easily cleanable, and free of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, pits, and free of difficult-to-clean internal corners and crevices.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
750.800b - The following food contact surfaces were soiled:
 A) soda nozzles at drive thru (mold);   and
B) quasadilla spatula (soiled and stored in the crevice between counters) - spatula was taken to dish area to go through ware washing.

Clean and sanitize food contact surfaces between uses/as needed, up to every 4hrs after continuous use, to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris.
Do not store utensils in the crevices between pieces of equipment.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.citation_text:
750.880 - Sleeves of cups were observed in the cabinet below the drive thru handsink. Moisture was present in the cabinet and on the sleeves. Cups were removed from the cabinet.

Single service items shall be stored, handled, and dispensed in a manner that protects items from potential contamination. Do not store single service items, clean equipment or food under the plumbing of sinks.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.citation_text:
750.1060 - Moisture was observed on the dining room soda counter around the lid holder. Moisture was also observed in the compartment beneath used to house the motor and soda lines. Puddling water was present in the ledge where the doors sit as well. The leak appeared to be coming from the waste tray drain line. Manager noted a call for service will be made for Pepsi to come check the machine.

Plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code.
Drain lines from equipment shall not discharge waste water in such a manner as will permit the flooding of floors or the flowing of water across working or walking areas or into difficult-to-clean areas, or otherwise create a nuisance.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text:
750.1200 & 1220 - A) Floor drains/covers were soiled in the following areas:
1. inside the water heater closet (debris);
2. between 3 part sink and dish racks (food debris/general buildup);
3. under the mini make line by the drive thru (food/general debris);   and
4. under the dining room drink counter (mold).
Clean floor drains and covers daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

B) Floors were observed to be soiled with general buildup of debris in the following areas:
1. in the water heater closet;
2. corner behind handsink next to tortilla storage shelves;
3. corners/along wall under dining room drink counter;  and
4. under walkin freezer shelves.
Clean the floors in the above mentioned areas and throughout along walls/in corners and under equipment daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

C) Grout at tiles around the fryer and thermolizer and in the dish area has worn down over time. Puddling liquid/oil and debris was observed. Re-grout around tiles in the aforementioned areas and throughout the facility where needed.

Floors must be in good repair, constructed to facilitate easy cleaning, and maintained clean.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.citation_text:
750.1210 & 1220 - A) Ceiling air exchange vent covers in the restrooms and above the make line near the tortilla storage shelves were soiled with dust buildup. Clean the ceiling vent covers as needed to eliminate buildup of dust.

B) Section of ceiling tile is missing above the handsink next to the tortilla storage shelves. Replace the missing section of ceiling tile.

C) Grease/food debris were observed along crevices at general surfaces of the tortilla grill, especially at both ends of the left bracket where gaps are present. Detail clean in areas where grease/food debris has accumulated and re-seal where gaps are present at the left bracket.

Walls and attached equipment must be in good repair, constructed to facilitate easy cleaning, and maintained clean.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.120 - Shredded cheese, diced tomatoes, and guacamole at cold table on main make line had internal temperatures of 50F-52F. Shift manager noted all products were at proper temperature at 7a after being removed from walkin cooler. Time control will be used until make line is repaired and able to maintain cold potentially hazardous foods (PHF) at 41F/below. GM made a call for service and noted a technician should be in for service some time today.

Cold PHF shall be maintained at a proper product temperature of 41F/below at all times during storage. **Make sure all employees understand time control policy - use or discard PHF on cold line within 4hrs of being removed from coolers holding product at 41F/below**

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.citation_text:
750.1120 - Paper towels were not available at handsink next to dry storage shelves. GM stocked the dispenser during the inspection.

Maintain supplies of soap and paper towels at handsinks to allow for proper handwashing.

findings.title: Presence of insects/rodents.  Animals prohibited
findings.citation_text:
750.1160 - Fruit flies were observed on the wall above the freeze machine and front counter handsink, on the wall above the drive thru window, and under the mini make line next to the drive thru. Several fruit flies came out of the floor drain under the mini make line when the cover was removed to expose heavy buildup of mold and debris. GM began cleaning the floor drain during the inspection. Use of fly strips was discussed with GM (see general comments). If cleaning alone does not alleviate the issue call the pest control operator for service.

Effective measures to minimize the presence of pests. Provide effective pest control.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.citation_text:
750.1210 - Walls were soiled with splash and/or general buildup around the freeze machine and drive thru soda machine, under the 3 part sink, and under the mini line by the drive thru.

Clean the walls under sinks and behind equipment daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
findings.citation_text:
750.1300 - Spray bottle in the mop closet labeled Kayquat Sanitizer had a blue liquid inside (possibly window cleaner). Chlorine and quat test strips were used to verify 0ppm concentration. Chemical in the bottle was not sanitizer. Shift Manager kept the bottle in the office to show GM. 

Containers of poisonous or toxic materials necessary for the maintenance of the establishment shall be labeled in accordance with law. Properly label containers of toxic substances.

**Make sure proper labels are kept on spray bottles to ensure staff are using appropriate chemicals for task being conducted. If pre-labeled spray bottles are to be used for a different chemical make sure the bottle and sprayer are thoroughly cleaned prior to putting another chemical in the bottle, and re-label the bottle to reflect the common name of the chemical inside**

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Observed the top door of the hot holding unit to not close properly or be properly fitting. Adjust door to repair or replace door.
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment:
Observed a wiping cloth stored in sanitizer bucket that contained water with 0 ppm sanitizer. Bucket water was replaced to have proper sanitizer solution for storing wiping cloth.
750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment:
Observed a single service container with dust inside. Cover or invert single service containers to protect the food contact surface.
750-880 Single-service articles shall be handled and dispensed in a manner which prevents contamination of surfaces which may come in contact with food or with the mouth of the user.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water disposed properly
findings.comment:
Observed a container of waste water under the handwashing sink near the drive thru window and soda machine. Water was disposed of.
750-1050 All water containing sewage shall be disposed of  properly either by a public sewage system or an approved private disposal system which is constructed and operated in conformance with applicable State and local laws, ordinances and regulations.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment:

750-1060 All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
1) Observed a missing ceiling tile in front of the walk in cooler door. Replace ceiling tile. 2) Observed baffles in frying area to be accumulating grease and oil. Clean the baffles. 3) observed the fans and ceiling to have dust in the walk in cooler. Clean the fans and ceiling.
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.
750-1220 Walls, ceilings, and attached fixtures shall be kept clean. Clean the walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Lighting provided as required.  Fixtures shielded
findings.comment:
Observed broken light shield over dry storage shelving. Replace light shield.
750-1240 All lights in the food prep, food storage or kitchen area of a establishment must be properly shielded (i.e. either have a physical shield or be a shatter resistant bulb) so as to reduce the potential for cross contamination in case of breakage.  Provide properly shielded lights.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment:
Three scoops were stored on top of three bulk food containers.  The top of the containers were soiled.  CORRECTED - managers immediately placed all three scoops and all three lids into dish area to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized.  If scoops are not stored within food, then they must be stored clean and dry, in a way that protects them from contamination.

750-280 Food dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with the handle extending out of the food; or stored clean and dry; or stored in running potable water dipper wells.
